name: Tin
occurrence: Mined mainly from cassiterite ore; historically alloyed with copper to make bronze, marking an entire age of human technology.
majorUses: Tin plating on steel cans (protects against corrosion)
notableCharacteristics: Undergoes 'tin pest' at very cold temperatures, transforming from strong metallic white tin into brittle, crumbly grey tin powder — historically blamed for buttons on Napoleon's soldiers' coats disintegrating in the Russian winter.
whyHere: Tin's two common oxidation states, +2 and +4, come from its position straddling typical metal and metalloid behaviour, and its allotropic transformation at low temperature (tin pest) reflects a genuine structural phase change between two different crystal forms.
didYouKnow: The 'tin pest' transformation from strong metal to crumbling powder in extreme cold is a real, documented phenomenon, historically theorized (though not conclusively proven) to have contributed to equipment failures during Napoleon's disastrous 1812 Russian campaign.
genZNote: Turns into brittle dust if it gets too cold. Also the reason your soldered electronics stay connected.
